d.competence: Learners are able to name the main vegetation zones, rivers and lakes of Africa and explain how people use rivers and lakes.
objectives: Describe the main vegetation zones of Africa.
Name the main rivers and lakes of Africa and locate them.
Explain the importance of African rivers and lakes.
recall: The climatic zones of Africa are repeated north and south of the Equator.
Africa has plateaux, basins, mountains and the Great Rift Valley.
Its soils include ferrallitic, ferruginous, desert, volcanic and alluvial soils.
d.recallNote: Check the homework: three big rivers and their mouths.
situation: Lake Chad, north of Cameroon, has become much smaller than it was sixty years ago. Fishermen and farmers who lived near it have lost their work.
Mariam wonders why this lake is shrinking while the big rivers of Africa, like the Congo, still carry so much water.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Lake Chad has become much smaller, and many fishermen and farmers have lost their work.
Who has been affected by the shrinking of Lake Chad?
The fishermen and farmers who lived near the lake have been affected.
What can be done to save Lake Chad?
People can use its water carefully, plant trees against desertification, and countries can work together to protect it.
d.justification: This lesson will help us to know the vegetation, rivers and lakes of Africa and their importance for people.

qa.q: Look at the map. Which vegetation covers the Congo Basin, and which covers most of Africa?
qa.a: The equatorial rainforest covers the Congo Basin. The savanna covers most of Africa.

qa.title: Question 2
qa.q: Why does the vegetation change from forest to savanna and then to desert as we move away from the Equator?
qa.a: The vegetation follows the rainfall. Rainfall decreases away from the Equator, so trees become fewer and shorter.

sum.title: I. Vegetation
sum.intro: The vegetation of Africa follows its climate. The main vegetation zones are the following:
items: A. Equatorial Rainforest
A thick evergreen forest covers the Congo Basin, southern Cameroon and the Guinea coast.
africa_vegetation.png
B. Savanna
Tall grasses with scattered trees cover most of Africa, north and south of the forest.
C. Semi-Desert and Desert
Thorny bushes and short grass grow in the Sahel. Deserts have almost no vegetation.
D. Mediterranean and Mountain Vegetation
Evergreen shrubs and trees grow in the far north and far south. Highlands have mountain forests and grasslands.

qa.q: Look at the map. Name the four largest rivers of Africa and the sea or ocean into which each flows.
qa.a: The Nile flows into the Mediterranean Sea, the Congo and the Niger into the Atlantic Ocean, and the Zambezi into the Indian Ocean.

qa.q: The River Benue, which flows through Garoua, is a tributary of which big river?
qa.a: The Benue is the main tributary of the River Niger. It joins the Niger at Lokoja in Nigeria.

qa.q: Lake Chad has no outlet to the sea: rivers flow into it, but no river flows out. What do we call this type of drainage?
qa.a: This is called inland drainage. The Chari and Logone rivers flow into Lake Chad.

qa.q: Give two ways in which people use African rivers and lakes.
qa.a: People use them for fishing, irrigation, transport and hydro-electricity, as at the Lagdo dam on the Benue and the Kariba dam on the Zambezi.

sum.title: II. Drainage
defs: Drainage is the system of rivers and lakes that carry water from the land to the sea or to inland lakes.
sum.intro: The main rivers and lakes of Africa are the following:
items: A. The Nile
The Nile is the longest river in Africa (about 6,650 km). It flows north into the Mediterranean Sea.
africa_drainage.png
B. The Congo
The Congo carries the most water of all African rivers. It flows into the Atlantic Ocean.
C. The Niger and the Zambezi
The Niger, with its tributary the Benue, flows into the Atlantic. The Zambezi forms the Victoria Falls and flows into the Indian Ocean.
D. Lakes
Lake Victoria is the largest lake in Africa. Lake Tanganyika is the deepest. Lake Chad has inland drainage and is shrinking.
E. Importance
Rivers and lakes are used for fishing, irrigation, transport and hydro-electricity, as at Lagdo and Kariba.

evaluation: Why does the vegetation of Africa change from the Equator to the tropics?
It changes because rainfall decreases from the Equator towards the tropics.
Into which sea does the Nile flow, and into which ocean does the Zambezi flow?
The Nile flows into the Mediterranean Sea, and the Zambezi flows into the Indian Ocean.
What is inland drainage? Give one example.
Inland drainage is when rivers flow into a lake that has no outlet to the sea, like Lake Chad.
remediation: The vegetation of the Congo Basin is the equatorial ______.
The vegetation that covers most of Africa is the ______.
The longest river of Africa is the ______.
The River Benue is a tributary of the River ______.
The largest lake of Africa is Lake ______.
The waterfalls on the Zambezi are the ______ Falls.
d.remediationAnswers: 1. rainforest 2. savanna 3. Nile 4. Niger 5. Victoria 6. Victoria
